name: Izakaya

origin.place: Nationwide; regional 'yakitori' in Higashimatsuyama, Muroran, Imabari

cells.what: Charcoal-grilled skewers, salt or sweet soy tare; in some towns 'yakitori' is pork
cells.seats: Counter, tables, or standing 'beer bar' style
cells.found: Everywhere, from standing bars to refined counters, festival stalls and convenience stores

cells.what: Tiny bars in narrow alleys, marked by red or white lanterns and a noren curtain
cells.seats: Often about ten; some take four or five

origin.place: Kitakyushu (said to have originated there); also Tokyo liquor shops
origin.era: linked by a Kitakyushu group to the 1901 Yawata steelworks

cells.what: Drinking at a liquor shop; distinct from standing bars run as restaurants
cells.seats: Standing, in or at the front of a liquor shop
cells.money: No prices confirmed; glasses and water are favours, not guaranteed
cells.found: Liquor shops; 94 in Kitakyushu in a 2018 survey

cells.what: Licensed street stalls serving food and drink at night
cells.seats: A few; best for two or three
cells.money: Mostly cash; most have no cover, bar-style stalls may

cells.what: Small bar, often run by a 'mama', with conversation and karaoke
cells.money: No official price data; check charges and time limits first
